sections.h2: Where does Northumberland County record deeds?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Register and Recorder at 201 Market Street, first floor, in Sunbury. The phone is 570-988-4143. On Mondays the office is open from 9:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., and Tuesday through Friday it runs 9:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. It closes every day from noon to 1:00 p.m.

One office holds two jobs here. It records land documents, and it also acts as register of wills for estates and issues marriage licenses. People selling an inherited house in Northumberland County therefore often deal with both counters in a single trip, first to open the estate and later to record the deed out of it.

Probate visits require an appointment, which you book by calling 570-988-4985. Recording does not, but the lunch closure means a package that arrives at 12:15 p.m. waits until 1:00.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Northumberland County?
sections.html:
The deed fee is $86.25 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025, and the same figure applies to taxable deeds, nontaxable deeds and quit claim deeds. That covers four pages, four names and one tract.

Northumberland County Recorder of Deeds charges since December 1, 2025
DocumentCharge
Deed (taxable, nontaxable or quit claim)$86.25
Mortgage$86.25
Satisfaction piece or release of mortgage$64.75
Assignment of mortgage$61.75
Easement$59.75
Power of attorney$18.50
Statement of Value$2.00
Notary bond and commission$39.00

Source: the county's Recorder of Deeds fee schedule. Extras are small: $2.00 for every page after four, $0.50 for each extra name and $0.50 for each extra tract except on mortgages. A marginal notation costs $2.00.

The office rejects a document when the fee is wrong, and the rejection applies even if the payment is too high. Count before writing the check.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax get paid on a Northumberland County sale?
sections.html:
Taxable deeds pay the state's 1 percent and a local 1 percent, plus the recording fee. Unlike some Pennsylvania counties, Northumberland states that separate checks are not required, so one check can cover all three.

The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue says the buyer and seller are both liable for the state tax. It also lists exempt transfers: certain moves between family members, transfers to government, and property that passes by will or intestate succession.

A deed that qualifies for an exemption still needs a Statement of Value, which is $2.00 here. If the deed claims an exemption, the title agent or attorney should name the reason on the form.

sections.h2: What paperwork rules apply in the Northumberland County recorder's office?
sections.html:
The county's requirements page is short, which makes the rules easy to follow and easy to trip over.

  • The document must be an original.
  • If the recorded deed is coming back by mail, include a self-addressed stamped envelope.
  • No blanket assignments or satisfaction pieces.
  • The correct recording fee is required, or the document is rejected.

Electronic filing is open for deeds, mortgages, assignments, satisfactions, releases of mortgage, UCC filings and powers of attorney. The county points filers to two vendors, CSC E-Recording Solutions and Simplifile, who register the submitting firm.

sections.h2: How does the register of wills affect selling an inherited house in Northumberland County?
sections.html:
An heir cannot sign a deed until someone has authority to act for the estate. In this county that authority comes from letters issued by the Register and Recorder, and the fee rises with the size of the estate.

  • Letters in an estate under $1,000 cost $142.75.
  • An estate between $50,001 and $100,000 costs $267.75.
  • Each additional $100,000, or fraction of it, adds $100.00.
  • Letters used for litigation only cost $102.75.

Those prices come from the December 2025 schedule and include the filing of the inventory and the inheritance tax return. The same office charges $50.00 for a certified copy of an instrument and $10.00 for a short certificate, which a title company may ask for. Call the office before the visit, since probate meetings run by appointment.

sections.h2: What does Northumberland County look like to a seller?
sections.html:
Northumberland County lies along the Susquehanna River in central Pennsylvania, formed in 1772 and now a fifth class county. Sunbury is the seat and the largest city, and Shamokin is the second city. It covers 478 square miles, of which 19 are water.

Anthracite mining and factories carried the local economy until the 1950s, when the mines began closing. Today the largest employers include Weis Markets, Knoebels Amusement Resort, the state government and Geisinger Health System. The Census Bureau puts the population at 89,920 for 2025, down 1.9 percent from the 2020 base.

Housing costs are low. The median owner-occupied home was valued at $162,400 for 2020 to 2024, median household income was $60,583, and 75.5 percent of homes are owner occupied. Montgomery County, by comparison, shows a median home value of $436,700.

sections.h2: Which places in Northumberland County do sellers come from?
sections.html:
Every town in the county records in the Sunbury office. Sunbury had 9,905 people in the 2010 census and Shamokin had 7,374, and Milton ranked third. The rest is a patchwork of boroughs, townships and small villages strung along the Susquehanna River and its West Branch, with mountains to the north and south and rolling hills in between.

The climate is humid continental. Sunbury averages about 27 degrees Fahrenheit in January and 73 in July, and Mount Carmel runs a couple of degrees cooler, which is worth remembering when you schedule showings and inspections in winter.

Because values are lower than in the Philadelphia suburbs, recording fees weigh more heavily on a small sale. An $86.25 deed fee is the same on a $90,000 house as on a $900,000 one, so closing cost estimates should show it as a line item rather than a rounding error.

sections.h2: How is an old mortgage cleared when a Northumberland County house sells?
sections.html:
The lender files a satisfaction piece or a release of mortgage with the recorder, and each costs $64.75 to record under the current schedule. A partial release costs the same. An assignment of a mortgage from one lender to another is $61.75.

The county refuses blanket satisfaction pieces, so each one has to name the specific mortgage it clears. If you are selling a house that still shows an old paid-off mortgage in the public record, ask the title company to find it. Ask the lender how long it takes to file, so the record is clear for the buyer.

sections.h2: What should I do before closing on a Northumberland County house?
sections.html:
Treat the recorder's office as a rules-driven stop and prepare for it.

  • Work out the exact fee from the schedule, including extra pages and names.
  • Bring a stamped, self-addressed return envelope.
  • Check the hours, including the noon closing.
  • Decide ahead whether the closing agent will file electronically through CSC or Simplifile.
  • For an inherited home, schedule the probate appointment well before the closing.

faqs.q: How much is the deed recording fee in Northumberland County?
faqs.a: A deed costs $86.25 to record, effective December 1, 2025, for up to four pages, four names and one tract. Extra pages cost $2 each and extra names $0.50 each.

faqs.q: Do I need separate checks for the deed and the transfer tax in Northumberland County?
faqs.a: No. The county says separate checks are not required for taxable deeds, so one check can cover the 1 percent state tax, the 1 percent local tax and the recording fee.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Northumberland County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts electronic deeds, mortgages, assignments, satisfactions, releases, UCC filings and powers of attorney through CSC E-Recording Solutions and Simplifile.

faqs.q: What hours is the Northumberland County recorder open?
faqs.a: Monday 9:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., and Tuesday through Friday 9:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. The office closes daily from noon to 1:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What happens if I send the wrong fee to the Northumberland County recorder?
faqs.a: The document is rejected, even when the payment is too high. Work out the exact fee from the current schedule before you send the deed.
